title: Irish man gets suspended sentence for threatening Jews in France
description: An Irish man was handed a suspended sentence of six months in prison for threatening to kill a Jewish person near Marseille in August, French media reported on Tuesday. The man, identified in La Provence and other French media as Patrick O’Brien, 60, was filmed in Avignon in August telling an Australian Jewish couple that he regretted Adolf Hitler had not “finished the job,” expressing hope for Hitler's return and threatening to shoot the woman in the head. He admitted intending to hurt the couple verbally after realizing that the man was Jewish. In court, he described himself as a “great humanist,” La Provence said. The Avignon court convicted him of glorifying crimes against humanity and making death threats aggravated by antisemitic prejudice. He was ordered to pay €500 ($556) to each victim and €300 ($333) to several civil-party organizations. The court rejected prosecutors' request to ban him from French territory for three years. A lawyer representing the victims, Annie Cohen, said the sentence was excessively lenient, La Provence reported, noting that the woman's father was a Holocaust survivor. The incident had attracted widespread attention in France after a video of the confrontation went viral in August.

title: Netherlands to boycott Eurovision 2027 over Israel's participation
description: The Netherlands is set to sit out the 2027 Eurovision Song Contest because of Israel’s participation, Dutch public broadcaster NPO announced on Tuesday. The announcement follows an earlier decision to return to the event after a one-year absence over the same issue. NPO chairwoman Jet de Ranitz said discussions with broadcasters had initially suggested that a Dutch entry was possible, but efforts to reach an agreement had failed. “Because of the sensitivities surrounding the issues currently at play, we have decided to take a step back,” she said, according to NOS , a major news broadcaster affiliated with NPO. The decision followed criticism of Israel’s military operations in Gaza. Several European broadcasters have called for Israel’s exclusion. In August, Dutch broadcaster AVROTROS announced it would boycott Eurovision for a second consecutive year, arguing that the competition could no longer be considered politically neutral. NPO said it would look into tasking a different broadcaster with organizing Dutch official participation in the event. However, the plan encountered significant resistance within the NPO's constituent bodies. Earlier this month, more than 400 NPO employees signed a letter protesting participation alongside Israel. The European Broadcasting Union, which organizes Eurovision, expressed regret over the Dutch decision but said it respected the broadcaster’s position, NOS reported. Ireland has also announced that it will boycott Eurovision in 2027, citing the humanitarian situation in Gaza. Unlike the Netherlands, Ireland will not broadcast the event. Israel finished second at the 2026 Eurovision Song Contest in Vienna, which was won by Bulgaria’s Dara.

Otzma Yehudit cited heavy crowding and unusually long wait times at polling stations across the Jewish state. The Central Elections Committee said high nationwide turnout "across all sectors of society" showed "strong public engagement in the democratic process." The committee said every voter who reaches a polling station by its closing time will be able to vote.

description: A former insurance executive in Ireland’s branch of the AIG firm who said his social media account had been hacked and used to vilify Jews is no longer with the company, his former boss recently told local Jews last week. AIG Ireland’s president and chief executive, Eric Andersen, informed the Jewish Representative Council of Ireland (JRCI) in an email of his firm’s parting of ways with John Gillick, former head of consumer marketing and sponsorship, The Irish Times reported on Sunday. Under Gillick’s account on X, text appeared last month that described Israel and Jews as “human scum” and Jews as “filthy dogs,” according to the report. One post stated: “Jews in Ireland need to be thrown out. They are traitors and land thieves. Our children need to be educated more about how evil Israel and Jews are,” and, “no one should associate with murdering jew war criminals.” On Sept. 2, a post on the account read: “I want to let people know that my account has been compromised by unauthorised person(s) and that recent posts containing anti-Semitic content were not written, published or endorsed by me,” and, “I unequivocally condemn the views expressed in those posts. They do not reflect my beliefs or values. I strongly oppose discrimination and hate in all forms.” Initially, AIG Ireland said the social media posts in question were “fraudulently published following the unauthorised compromise of an employee’s personal social media account.” However, in informing JCRI of Gillick’s departure, Andersen wrote that matter of the posts was the subject of an ongoing police investigation, and an internal one at AIG Ireland. JRCI Chair Orli Degani told The Irish Times that she did not know the circumstances surrounding Gillick’s departure, but welcomed AIG’s investigation, the newspaper reported.

During the immersive two-year program, fellows attend intensive in-person retreats, workshops and monthly online meetings and receive one-on-one mentoring sessions with Lazar and guest presenters. Lazar brings knowledge of Jewish and Western music and a deep understanding of the relationship between text and music that defines choral music. He models, encourages and nurtures the talents of a new generation of conductors of Jewish music. "The conductor integrates music, text and cultural identity with mastery and precision, creating inspiring and transformative musical moments," Lazar said. "The institute provides the specialized skills and knowledge needed to make all this possible." The inaugural group of fellows has completed the program. They were presented with a certificate in Jewish Choral Conducting and performed in a recital at the North American Jewish Choral Festival. The graduates are Shani Chamovitz, Abram Foster, Joshua Gonzalez, Matthew Gonzalez, Joel Herman, Dor Kaminka, Juliana Rappaport, Elliot Roman, Yoel Rubinstein, Nitzan Shohaam and Hadas Sturman. A new cohort of JCCI fellows recently began the program, continuing the mission to share the legacy of Jewish choral music with the next generation. "We are guided by a vision of vibrant Jewish identity through the study and performance of Jewish music at the highest level of excellence. Our goal is to create a pipeline of talented and knowledgeable conductors of Jewish choral music who will ensure the future of this rich and empowering art form," Lazar said. For more information, visit: www.zamirchoralfoundation.org .

title: Italy arrests Hamas advocate over street riots
description: Authorities in Italy last week arrested a 30-year-old academic who justified Hamas’s Oct. 7, 2023, massacres for allegedly organizing violent demonstrations in Milan inspired by riots in France. A dual citizen of Italy and Morocco, Siher was the administrator of the Instagram page “Movimento 17 Ottobre” ("October 17 Movement"), which called for demonstrations across Italy. Siher, an organizer of Palestinian anti-Israel actions of Italy, in a 2024 essay defended the Hamas-led terrorist attacks in southern Israel on Oct. 7, 2023, the report said. He wrote in the magazine Miccia : "Few in the West were able to conceive without ifs and buts of ‘Operation Al-Aqsa Flood’ for what it was: a revolutionary act of decolonization.” "Operation Al-Aqsa Flood" is the name that Hamas gave its rampage, in which terrorists killed some 1,200 people and abducted 251 others, amid other war crimes.   Siher had no criminal record before his arrest, the report said. His wife is under investigation on suspicion of the same offenses attributed to him. The Milan clashes are part of the apparent spread of rioting that began in France several weeks ago. Italian authorities have detained more than 370 people over the weekend and arrested nine in connection with the riots, in which far-left agitators have taken to the streets along with other protesters, many of African and Middle Eastern descent, to protest a diverse range of issues, from underfunding of education to racism in society. Similar protests have begun to occur in Spain, where authorities in Barcelona detained more than 100 people over the weekend.

It is believed the graffiti was sprayed in the early hours of Tuesday, October 20," a spokesperson for Lancashire Police told the Blackpool Gazette on Friday. The bishop of Blackburn, Philip North, was among the prominent officials who condemned the incident, which police are investigating as a hate crime, the report said. North called the incident "an assault on the values of respect, dignity and freedom of religion," and called for an "unwavering rejection of antisemitism." Rachel Tax, president of the Blackpool Reform Jewish Congregation, told the paper: “My feelings when I first saw it were horror, disbelief and sadness. The graffiti also included two lightning bolts, resembling the Nazi SS insignia, and the number 1488, a neo-Nazi code combining the white supremacist “14 Words” slogan with “88,” representing “Heil Hitler,” according to the Blackpool Lead.

The planned operation reportedly included attacks on nuclear facilities, power plants and other infrastructure. According to the newspaper, the offensive did not go ahead because Trump opposed resuming hostilities before the U.S. midterm elections on Nov. 3. One source said Israel and the United States could still resume military operations in the coming weeks. In the INN interview, Netanyahu said he had instructed the IDF and the Mossad to bring down the Iranian regime. He said Iran and its "axis of evil" were "weaker than ever." description: “Israel Undiplomatic” brings sharp insight and spirited debate to the stories shaping Israel and the Middle East. Hosted by JNS senior contributing editor Ruthie Blum and former ambassador Mark Regev, both former advisers to the Prime Minister’s Office, the show goes beyond talking points to tackle Israel’s toughest political, diplomatic and security dilemmas head-on. From Gaza ceasefire negotiations to U.S.-Israel relations and from Iran’s nuclear ambitions to the war on terror, Blum and Regev dissect the week’s headlines with authority, candor and a touch of humor. What sets “Israel Undiplomatic” apart is the dynamic between its hosts: Two seasoned insiders often agree on the goals but clash on the details. Their conversations reveal how even shared worldviews can lead to different conclusions about policy, diplomacy and the future of Israel. Whether analyzing the latest Middle East peace proposals, exposing Western double standards or weighing the political fallout of Israel’s military actions, “Israel Undiplomatic” delivers smart, unscripted dialogue that cuts through spin and gets to the truth. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu told Army Radio on Wednesday that the portfolio should stay with his Likud Party. "IDF soldiers need to go into battle knowing that they are fighting a just war," Ben-Gvir, who currently serves as the Jewish state's national security minister, wrote on X in Hebrew. The WJC organized the forum in partnership with the European Commission. During the forum, U.S. Special Envoy to Monitor and Combat Antisemitism Rabbi Yehuda Kaploun announced that Armenia and three additional countries are expected to join the International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance (IHRA), according to the WJC. title: Is Jewish unity in a polarized nation possible?
description: At a time when most Americans have lost the ability to listen to people with opposing views on political issues, how can a fractious Jewish community that is also split on denominational lines pull together? That’s the question posed by JNS editor-in-chief Jonathan Tobin. He believes that Jewish disunity has been exacerbated by the capture of the political left, which is still supported by the majority of Jews, by anti-Israel and antisemitic “progressives.” This puts even more pressure on Jewish liberals to conform to fashionable opinion on the left that poses a threat to their community’s interests and safety. He’s joined in this week’s episode of “Think Twice” by DePaul University Law professor Roberta Kwall, author of the new book , Polarized: Why American Jews Are Divided And What to Do About It . She believes that a vital Jewish center can be reconstituted if people realize that what unites them is still greater than those who seek to tear them apart. Part of the problem is that Israel, which was once thought to be a unifying factor, is now the greatest source of division, with many unaffiliated or liberal Jews no longer supportive of it, and a small but well-publicized minority actively opposed to Zionism. At the core of her effort is a statement of largely anodyne principles that she believes the overwhelming majority of Jews agree on. Among them is support for the right of Israel to exist as a Jewish and democratic state, as well as the legitimacy of criticizing its government. But for Kwall, equally important is the need to re-emphasize education and the importance of tradition to reinforce Jewish identity. In such a context, it will be easier for Jews who disagree on politics or aspects of Israeli policy to listen to each other and find common ground.
